items.q: Two days after neck surgery, calcium is low, phosphate is high and PTH is suppressed. Which explanation best fits all three values?
items.exp: Low calcium with high phosphate and low PTH identifies deficient PTH secretion; postsurgical disease is the most common cause listed. (Book p884)

items.q: For hypocalcemia, the chapter first organizes causes using serum ___ and ___.
items.exp: The cause tree is based on phosphate and PTH, after confirming true hypocalcemia. (Book p884)

items.q: An adult with mucocutaneous candidiasis and ectodermal abnormalities develops low-PTH hypocalcemia without surgery. Which syndrome fits?
items.exp: APECED means autoimmune polyendocrinopathy–candidiasis–ectodermal dystrophy and corresponds to APS/PGA type 1. (Book p884)

items.q: Match the following DiGeorge clues — 1) Gene 2) Chromosomal region 3) Immune-organ defect … A) TBX1 B) Thymic hypoplasia C) 22q11.2 deletion
items.exp: DiGeorge syndrome is linked to TBX1 and 22q deletion; thymic hypoplasia explains its immune component. (Book p884)

items.q: Which is the odd one out in the CATCH22 feature set?
items.exp: CATCH22 comprises cardiac defects, abnormal facies, thymic hypoplasia, cleft palate and hypocalcemia with 22q deletion; deficient parathyroid development, not hyperplasia, explains the calcium finding. (Book p884)

items.q: A neonate has a conotruncal heart defect, cleft palate and hypocalcemic seizures. Which additional finding most strongly supports the same syndrome?
items.exp: This is the CATCH22 constellation of DiGeorge syndrome; thymic hypoplasia is the discriminating associated finding. (Book p884)

items.q: Evaluate: I CKD-related secondary HPT requires suppressed PTH. II Low calcium with high phosphate and high PTH can occur in CKD.
items.exp: The elevated PTH is a compensatory response in CKD, unlike low-PTH hypoparathyroidism. (Book p884)

items.q: Match the following — 1) Postsurgical gland loss 2) CKD secondary HPT 3) AKI … A) Low Ca/high phosphate with high PTH B) Low Ca/high phosphate with acute renal dysfunction C) Low Ca/high phosphate with low PTH
items.exp: The page separates deficient secretion after surgery from secondary HPT in CKD and the acute renal failure branch. (Book p884)

items.q: Which cause does not belong in the cellular-stress branch of hypocalcemia with phosphate release?
items.exp: Tumor lysis, muscle breakdown and hemolysis release intracellular phosphate. Isolated gland excision instead reduces PTH secretion. (Book p884)

items.q: A patient with abdominal pain and vomiting is found to have acute pancreatitis and low calcium. Which interpretation follows the chapter's warning?
opts: Symptoms may resemble hypercalcemia despite a low measured calcium
Abdominal symptoms establish hypercalcemia despite the result
Low calcium rules out pancreatitis as the underlying diagnosis
Pancreatitis must suppress PTH to cause these symptoms
items.exp: The page warns that pancreatitis can mimic hypercalcemic abdominal symptoms while investigations show hypocalcemia. (Book p884)

items.q: In the low-calcium/high-phosphate branch with normal or raised PTH, the non-cell-lysis systemic infection listed is ___.
items.exp: Sepsis appears beside cellular stress and pancreatitis in the normal/high-PTH branch; the tree does not imply that every cause has identical phosphate values in every patient. (Book p884)
